voice.check.replay: Right now, I’m showing you a replay of August 25, 2025.
voice.check: Hi. I’m here to help you figure out where the smoke is coming from. It only takes a minute. If you smell smoke, tap the big blue button: I smell smoke. And if you ever see flames, call nine-one-one right away.
voice.check.install: To keep me on your phone, tap: {add}.
voice.q1: Let’s start. Take a look outside, toward the smell. Do you see flames? If you do, tap the red {yes} button. If you don’t, tap {no}. If you can’t tell, tap {notSure}.
voice.q2: Now look at the sky. Which picture looks like your sky? The first picture is dark smoke rising from one spot: {column}. The second is grey haze hanging everywhere: {haze}. The third is for when you can’t see any smoke, or it’s dark out: {smell}. If you can’t tell, tap {notSure}.
voice.q3: Last question. Is anything burning nearby? Tap what you see. {firePit}. {mulch}. {people}. {other}. If nothing is burning, tap {nothing}. If you can’t tell, tap {notSure}.
voice.nearby: Okay. A neighbour’s fire pit or bonfire may explain the smell. If it’s out of control, or if burning is banned right now, tap the big red button to call nine-one-one. To check the drifting smoke anyway, tap: {check}.
voice.location: Now, where are you? The easiest way is to tap the blue button, Use my location, and say yes when your phone asks. Or type your town in the box, and tap it in the list.
voice.loading: Thanks. Give me a few seconds. I’m following the wind backward, hour by hour, to see where your air came from.
voice.loading.waking: The smoke engine is waking up. This can take a minute.
voice.verdict.drifting: Okay, here’s what I found. The smoke you’re smelling is most likely drifting from {fire}, about {distance} {direction} of you.
voice.verdict.drifting.under: Okay, here’s what I found. The smoke you’re smelling is most likely drifting from {fire}, less than one kilometre from you.
voice.verdict.drifting.far: So it’s most likely smoke carried by the wind from far away.
voice.verdict.unclear: Okay, here’s what I found. It could be smoke drifting from {fire}, but the air passed {distance} from it, so I can’t be sure. It might also be something close by. Please take a look outside.
voice.verdict.unclear.wind: Okay, here’s what I found. It could be smoke drifting from {fire}. The air passed {distance} from it, but the wind shifted, so I can’t be sure. It might also be something close by. Please take a look outside.
voice.verdict.unexplained: Okay, here’s what I found. I didn’t find a known fire where your air came from. That doesn’t mean there’s no fire. It could be something close by, like a new fire, a brush pile, or wood smoke. Please take a look outside.
voice.verdict.confidence.medium: I’m fairly confident, but not completely.
voice.verdict.reason.heights: the air at different heights took different paths
voice.verdict.notice: The fire is close to you. Please follow official instructions. If you’ve been told to leave, tap: {link}.
voice.verdict.aq: Air quality right now: {risk}. Here’s the official advice: {advice}
voice.verdict.aq.none: I don’t have an air quality reading from the last two hours. For the official advice, tap: {link}.
voice.verdict.break: If the air inside gets uncomfortable, a library or community centre with filtered air can help. Tap: Find a library near me.
voice.verdict.nurse: If you feel unwell but it’s not an emergency, you can call eight-one-one to talk to a nurse.
voice.verdict.call: And if you ever see flames or a smoke column, tap the red button at the bottom to call nine-one-one.
voice.card.drifting: Drifting smoke, most likely from {fire}, about {distance} {direction} of you.
voice.card.drifting.under: Drifting smoke, most likely from {fire}, less than one kilometre from you.
voice.card.unclear: It’s unclear. It may be smoke from {fire}, or something close by. Please take a look outside.
voice.card.unexplained: Unexplained smoke. I found no known fire where your air came from. Please take a look outside.
voice.card.noFires: Unexplained smoke. No fire is reported within {km} kilometres of you. Please take a look outside.
voice.card.badges: Under the answer are its sources. Tap one to see where it comes from: {fire}. {trace}. {alert}.
voice.card.why: For the details and what to do, tap the {why} button.
voice.card.call: If you see flames or a smoke column, tap the big red button at the bottom to call nine-one-one.
voice.emergency: Okay. Let’s call nine-one-one now. Tap the big white button at the bottom. When they answer, tell them where you are, what you see, which way it’s moving if you can tell, and if anyone needs help. If the screen shows your location, you can read it to them. Stay on the line, and if the fire is close, move away while you talk. You’re doing the right thing. If officials told you to leave, tap: {leave}.
voice.leave.where: If officials told you to leave your home, first tell us where you are. Tap: Use my location, or type your town.
voice.leave.intro: If you’re told to leave, leave right away. Follow emergency alerts and local radio.
voice.leave.near: I’m here to help you leave. Please leave right away when officials tell you to, and keep listening to emergency alerts and local radio. Here’s where to go: the reception centre is {name}, at {address}. When you get there, register first, so officials know you’re accounted for. Tap: Get directions, and your phone’s map will guide you. If you have time, take your medication, wallet and ID, keys, phone and charger, glasses, and your pets. Don’t delay for anything else. Once you’re on your way, tap: Tell family you’re OK, and I’ll help you send them a message with your location.
voice.leave.far: This evacuation was for people near {fire}, {distance} from {town}, so it doesn’t apply to you.
voice.leave.far.links: If officials ever ask you to leave, they’ll announce where to go on the links below.
voice.leave.far.211: You can also call two-one-one for help.
voice.leave.none.links: For a fire happening now, officials announce where to go on the links below.
voice.leave.211: You can also call two-one-one for shelters and help.
voice.how: Here’s how it works. You tell us where you are. Using hourly wind data, we trace the air arriving at your spot backward in time. We check whether it passed near a fire that satellites or officials know about. Then we give you an answer, and the official air quality advice. One important thing: a fire that just started may not show up in satellite data for hours. So if you see flames or a smoke column, call nine-one-one. Don’t wait for an answer from the app.
voice.locationOff: Your location is turned off. That’s fine. Type the name of your town in the box, then tap: Check this place.
voice.noData: We can’t check the air right now. That doesn’t mean there’s no fire. Please look outside. If you see flames or a smoke column, tap the red Call nine-one-one button at the bottom of the screen. You can tap: Try again, in a moment.

todo.title: What to do
advice.general.low: Ideal air quality for outdoor activities.
advice.general.moderate: No need to modify your usual outdoor activities unless you experience symptoms such as coughing and throat irritation.
advice.general.high: Consider reducing or rescheduling strenuous activities outdoors if you experience symptoms such as coughing and throat irritation.
advice.general.very_high: Reduce or reschedule strenuous activities outdoors, especially if you experience symptoms such as coughing and throat irritation.

how.title: How it works
how.intro: We look at where the air around you has been over the last day, and whether it passed a fire.
how.step1: You tell us where you are
how.step1.body: Share your location, or type your town.
how.step2.body: Using hourly wind data, we step the air arriving at your spot back in time, one hour per step.
how.step3: We check for fires along the way
how.step3.before: At every step we measure the
how.step3.after: : the shortest distance between the air and each active fire.
how.step3.forward: We also trace the fire’s smoke forward: when the air coming to you and the smoke leaving the fire meet, it supports the answer.
how.diagramAria: Diagram: the air’s hourly path passes a fire; the closest approach is the shortest distance between them
how.drifting.body: The air passed within 25 km of an active fire.
how.unclear.body: It passed 25 to 50 km from a fire, or the wind was unsteady.
how.unexplained.body: No active fire within 50 km of the air’s path.
how.aqhi: We add the Air Quality Health Index so you know what to do right now.
how.firms.body: Satellite fire detections (VIIRS and MODIS), several times a day as satellites pass over
how.eccc.body: Air Quality Health Index and air quality alerts
how.limits.body: A fire that just started may not show up in satellite data for hours. If you see flames or a smoke column, call 911. Don’t wait for a verdict.
